amortization.heading: What do extra payments change on the same loan?
amortization.intro: On this hypothetical $100,000 loan at 6% over ten years, the no-extra schedule takes 120 payments and $33,224.60 in interest. Adding $100 monthly changes that to 107 payments and $29,328.37 in interest.
notes: The original principal, nominal annual rate and contractual term are unchanged. The model holds the scheduled principal-and-interest payment constant, then adds the selected extra principal at each stated payment month.

The monthly $100 and annual $1,200 cases have the same annual extra budget during a complete year, but different timing. Earlier principal reduction changes interest. Their final years and capped last payments need not use the same total extra cash.
The displayed first payment includes any extra due in month 1; it is not always the scheduled principal-and-interest amount. A one-time payment in month 12 has no effect before that month.

No payment penalties, fees, escrow, taxes, insurance or loan recast are included. Dates label monthly periods; this is not an actual-day lender payoff quote. All currency is USD, with fractional cents retained internally and display rounding at the end.
amortization.summary: An amortization schedule separates each payment into interest, principal and the remaining balance. In the controlled example below, adding $100 monthly shortens the original ten-year loan by 13 payments while leaving the scheduled principal-and-interest installment unchanged.

credit-card-minimum-payment.heading: How do minimum-only, extra and fixed payments compare?
credit-card-minimum-payment.intro: For this hypothetical $5,000 balance at 24% APR, a 2%-of-opening-balance minimum plus monthly interest and a $25 floor starts at $200. Minimum-only repayment takes 138 months and $4,625.07 in interest. Adding $50 above each changing minimum takes 53 months and $2,273.94 in interest.

rows.label: Recalculate and pay only the minimum

notes: The first three rows use the same changing minimum rule: opening balance × 2% plus monthly interest, or $25 if larger, capped at the amount owed. Each fixed extra is added above the newly calculated minimum every month.

Minimum plus $50 and a fixed $250 total begin with the same $250 payment, but their later budgets differ. The minimum-plus-extra payment generally declines; the fixed-total strategy keeps paying $250 until its capped final payment. This is not an equal-lifetime-budget comparison.
The fixed-total row opens the existing Credit Card Payoff Calculator. It is a separate calculation task, not another name or mode for the changing-minimum tool.

No new purchases, fees, rate changes or multiple balances are included. Both calculations use monthly APR/12 interest and retain fractional cents. Your agreement and statement may use daily balances, other minimum rules and different rounding.
credit-card-minimum-payment.summary: A minimum payment follows the rule entered from your agreement. Paying extra above that changing minimum and keeping a fixed total monthly payment are different strategies; the comparison below shows their different payoff times and interest under the same starting balance and APR.
